intent: Research sealed counterfactual lead MS-0119 as an Evidence-first inventory-amplification packet for the 2021-2023 memory downturn. Preserve end-market consumption, customer ship-in/procurement, customer inventory, supplier inventory, supplier bit supply, wafer starts/utilization and price as distinct claim scopes. Test whether customer inventory correction caused DRAM/NAND procurement to fall below end-market consumption and whether supplier inventory accumulation then elicited production cuts, while preserving genuine macro/end-demand weakness as a separate concurrent mechanism. Do not claim pull-forward, double ordering, causal weights or a single 'demand collapse' scalar unless directly supported by claim-scoped primary or methodological-primary evidence.
rationale_summary: The campaign maturity index identifies customer-side inventory disclosures as a thin area, and sealed lead MS-0119 specifically challenges the reduction of the 2022 downturn to end-demand collapse. Primary supplier materials already expose the required separation: customers reduced DRAM/NAND procurement below end-market consumption while correcting inventory, suppliers accumulated inventory as supply exceeded demand, and producers subsequently cut wafer starts. Existing Evidence and research-hypothesis owners are sufficient; no new semantic owner is required for the Evidence-first phase.
